import os
import sys
from io import StringIO

import pytest

import click


@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="Bug is Linux-specific")
def test_prompt_backspace_linux(monkeypatch):
    # Simulate a Linux terminal where readline is active
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.stdin, "isatty", lambda: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.stdout, "isatty", lambda: True)

    # Simulate user input: type "hello", then backspace once, then enter
    # The bug causes backspace to remove two characters, so "he" would remain.
    # The fix should result in "hell".
    input_stream = StringIO("hello\b\n")
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "stdin", input_stream)

    # Capture stdout to ensure no unexpected output, though the core of the bug
    # is the returned value.
    output_stream = StringIO()
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "stdout", output_stream)

    # The expected behavior is that one backspace removes one character.
    # So, "hello" + backspace should yield "hell".
    result = click.prompt("Enter something")

    assert result == "hell"
